evidence:
Overall the rubric is strongly outcome-based: almost every criterion names a browser-observable state change plus readback (independent contexts, restart_app, document.activeElement, getBoundingClientRect, 15-second no-reload waits, replays with 'nothing changes' readbacks, 401/404 status where hireops_rules.md section 1 makes them public). Unique suffixed titles/names are required (functional prompt.md:15, polish prompt.md:14). No criterion grades source, a 'looks right' impression (other than the visual Likert craft rows, which are judgement by design and acceptable per SKILL known false positives), or a response shape without state change. Lena's '1 unread' baseline in hro_unread_counts (functional judge.toml:335) is correct from the seed (APP-301 has 3 messages REC3,CAN3,REC3; USR-CAN3 read_count 2). 

DEFECT (non-distinctive ordering probes). The arrival-order rows use probes whose expected order coincides with creation order (and with the alphabetical order of the placeholder labels), so they cannot distinguish the public rule 'a card that arrives in a stage goes to the bottom' / 'arrive ... in board order' (hireops_rules.md:57-58, 89-91) from a plausible broken implementation that keeps each card's original insertion position (or sorts stages by creation time/id/name):
(1) hro_arrive_bottom, functional judge.toml:64-66: 'M: B, moved into a Screen that already holds A, lands below A.' Protocol M (prompt.md:27,29) adds A then B, then moves A then B into Screen, so creation order = bottom-arrival order. The distinctive observation available in M (A moved back Interview->Screen must land BELOW B) is never directed to be read; same in L (B into Interview below A, again creation order).
(2) hro_bulk_move, functional judge.toml:208-210: 'three selected cards ... arrive at the bottom of that stage in their board order.' Protocol B step (3) (prompt.md:35) selects Y,W,X from Applied V,W,X,Y,Z with no prior re-order in Applied, so board order = creation order = alphabetical order; it only distinguishes selection order. All bulk moves in B take cards from a single stage, so the cross-stage 'by stage then by place' board order is never probed either.
(3) hro_add_candidate, functional judge.toml:37-38 'in the order added' -- inherent for adds, but combined with labels A..F/V..Z an alphabetical-sort app also passes.
The other ordering rows are distinctive and good: hro_undo_restores (V back at top, W,X,Y back above Z and A's J2 card, distinct from bottom-append) and hro_reorder/hro_interview_reorder_free (manual order). 

Minor decidability notes (not separately failing, recorded for reconciliation): (a) hro_job_open (judge.toml:29) needs a replay with a Recruiter's account as hiring manager; an app whose UI never exposes a Recruiter's identifier in the observed request vocabulary leaves that leg hard to construct (prompt.md:17 forbids unobserved routes). Rafael's own /me-style response usually supplies it, so P3 at most. (b) hro_seen (judge.toml:353) second half: protocol U (prompt.md:41) states the no-reload rule only for Rafael's page, so whether Tomas's page may be reloaded before reading 'seen' is not explicit; the rule (hireops_rules.md:117-119) says seen marks arrive by themselves. (c) hro_candidate_private (judge.toml:389) leak detection relies on judge-created note text and rejection reason, but neither prompt requires those strings be distinctive, and protocol K does not explicitly direct inspecting candidate responses during the window while Tomas's card is rejected. These are bounded; the judge can still decide them in most runs.

Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json entries are scripted golden observations only; no configured judge run exists, so no criterion's actual judge decidability was measured. That missing measurement remains a risk and is not waived.
counterexample: Broken app that could pass: each card gets a fixed position number when created (A=1, B=2, ...) and stage lists are always sorted by that number; only explicit up/down re-ordering swaps numbers. Moving a card into a non-empty stage therefore inserts it by its old number, not at the bottom (violates hireops_rules.md:57-58 and 89-91). In protocol M, B moved into Screen holding A lands below A -> hro_arrive_bottom passes (weight 1). In protocol B step 3, Y,W,X arrive below V as W,X,Y -> hro_bulk_move passes (weight 1.5). Undo/restart/live-board rows also pass because the server order is consistent. The real defect would show only if the judge happened to read Screen after A returns from Interview in M (A would appear above B), which no criterion or protocol step directs.
suggested_fix: Make the ordering probes distinctive: in protocol M direct the judge to move A back Interview->Screen and read that A is now BELOW B, and grade that in hro_arrive_bottom; in protocol B re-order Applied (e.g. move Y above W) before the multi-card move and include one cross-stage selection, so the expected board-order arrival differs from creation/alphabetical/selection order.
